arxiv-2109-12709.title: Automated Multi-Process CTC Detection using Deep Learning
arxiv-2109-12709.creator: Authors: Elena Ivanova, Kam W. Leong, and Andrew F. Laine
arxiv-2109-12709.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Authors: Elena Ivanova, Kam W. Leong, and Andrew F. Laine. Circulating Tumor Cells (CTCs) bear great promise as biomarkers in tumor prognosis. However, the process of identification and later enumeration of CTCs require manual labor, which is error-prone and time-consuming. The recent developments in object detection via Deep Learning using Mask-RCNNs and wider availability of pre-trained models have enabled sensitive tasks with limited data of such to be tackled with unprecedented accuracy.

arxiv-2307-04931.title: Modelling the effect of 3D temperature and chemistry on the cross-correlation signal of transiting ultra-hot Jupiters: A study of 5 chemical species on WASP-76b 2023 Modelling the effect of 3D temperature and chemistry on the cross-correlation signal of transiting ultra-hot Jupiters: A study of 5 ch
arxiv-2307-04931.creator: Joost P. Wardenier, Vivien Parmentier, Michael R. Line, Elspeth K. H. Lee
arxiv-2307-04931.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Joost P. Wardenier, Vivien Parmentier, Michael R. Line, Elspeth K. H. Lee. Ultra-hot Jupiters are perfect targets for transmission spectroscopy. However, their atmospheres feature strong spatial variations in temperature, chemistry, dynamics, cloud coverage, and scale height. This makes transit observations at high spectral resolution challenging to interpret. In this work, we model the cross-correlation signal of five chemical species – Fe, CO, H 2 {}_{\text{2}} O, OH, and TiO – on WASP-76b, a benchmark ultra-hot Jupiter.

arxiv-2311-05241.title: When Meta-Learning Meets Online and Continual Learning: A Survey
arxiv-2311-05241.creator: Jaehyeon Son, Soochan Lee, and Gunhee Kim
arxiv-2311-05241.description: Abstract Over the past decade, deep neural networks have demonstrated significant success using the training scheme that involves mini-batch stochastic gradient descent on extensive datasets. Expanding upon this accomplishment, there has been a surge in research exploring the application of neural networks in other learning scenarios. One notable framework that has garnered significant attention is meta-learning .

arxiv-2311-16911.title: Diffusive Evaporation Dynamics in Polymer Solutions is Ubiquitous
arxiv-2311-16911.creator: Max Huisman, Wilson C. K. Poon, Patrick B. Warren, Simon Titmuss, Davide Marenduzzo
arxiv-2311-16911.description: Abstract Recent theory and experiments have shown how the buildup of a high-concentration polymer layer at a one-dimensional solvent-air interface can lead to an evaporation rate that scales with time as t − 1 / 2 t^{-1/2} and that is insensitive to the ambient humidity.

arxiv-2502-09881.title: Model theory of homogeneous D-sets Thanks: The second author was supported by the grant INV-2023-162-2840 from the Faculty of Sciences of the Universidad de los Andes while carrying out this research
arxiv-2502-09881.creator: Felipe Estrada and John Goodrick
arxiv-2502-09881.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Felipe Estrada and John Goodrick. We explore several model-theoretic aspects of D D -sets, which were studied in detail by Adeleke and Neumann. We characterize ultrahomogeneity in the class of colored D D -sets and classify unbounded order-indiscernible sequences in such structures. We use these results to provide a characterization of distal colored D D -sets and prove that all colored D D -sets with quantifier elimination are dp-minimal.

arxiv-2511-01720.title: Efficient Tool-Calling Multi-Expert NPC Agent for Commonsense Persona-Grounded Dialogue
arxiv-2511-01720.creator: Mahammad Nuriyev
arxiv-2511-01720.description: Abstract We present a multi-expert system for creating Non-Player Characters (NPCs) capable of both natural dialogue and contextual action execution in interactive environments. Our approach leverages Qwen3 as the base model with specialized Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters to create three distinct expert modules: tool calling, tool response interpretation, and direct dialogue.

pmc-11695448.title: Central nervous system relapse after allogeneic HCT in FLT3-mutated AML
pmc-11695448.creator: Khouloud Kouidri, Fabian Acker, Rosa Toenges, Saskia Pfaff, Sarah Lindner, Julia Riemann, Marek Werth, Salem Ajib, Fabian Lang, Björn Steffen, Thomas Oellerich, Hubert Serve, Anjali Cremer, Gesine Bug
pmc-11695448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Central nervous system (CNS) relapse in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is rare, but prognostically extremely unfavorable and associated with very high mortality rates. Aim of our single-center study was to define risk factors for CNS relapse in patients with FLT3-mutated AML after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) and to determine the impact of pre-emptive or salvage therapy with FLT3-inhibitors (FLT3i) on occurrence of CNS relapse and overall prognosis.

pmc-12569346.creator: Ghanwa Imran, Umair Ali, Muddassir Khalid
pmc-12569346.description: Plastic packaging is produced through a process called polymerization, where monomers (the building blocks) are linked together. Usually, monomers are stable in the polymer chain; however, the presence of low molecular weight substances, such as LDPE, prevents the monomers from being packaged closely.

pmc-13067805.title: Ganoderma lucidum mediates microglial polarization and ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by reducing oxidative stress and inhibiting NF-κB/STAT3 pathway
pmc-13067805.creator: Lu Zhang, Jie Chen, Sauchu Yuen, Meiling Wu, Wenting Li, Shenyu Yan, Jiangang Shen
pmc-13067805.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a neuroinflammatory disease affecting the central nervous system (CNS), for which effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Ganoderma Lucidum (GL) is a nature healthy food supplement whose effects on MS remain unknown. Using an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model, we tested the hypothesis that GL could mitigate MS by inhibiting microglial activation and promoting a shift toward an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype.

pmc-13115623.title: Over Two Million Life-Years at Risk: Why Gaza’s Health Reconstruction Is a Moral Imperative
pmc-13115623.creator: Alessandro Vitale, Mohammad Abu Hilal, Umberto Cillo, Isabella Frigerio, Andrew A. Gumbs
pmc-13115623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? The concept of Healthocide frames the systematic destruction of healthcare infrastructure, workforce, and services in Gaza as a deliberate determinant of population health collapse.The resulting disruption to care, disease prevention, and survival conditions has already led to an estimated loss of over three million life-years since October 2023. Public health significance—Why is this work of significance to public health?

pmc-13403601.title: The association between the advanced lung cancer inflammation index and successful antegrade recanalization in patients with coronary chronic total occlusion: a retrospective cross-sectional study
pmc-13403601.creator: Bingyang Qi, Mengyang Liu, Xin Yi, Yanyao Jia, Yahang Tan, Zhiyong Zhang, Tao Zhang, Zhichang Zheng, Chuang Li, Yuan Fu, Jing Cheng, Lin Zhao
pmc-13403601.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChronic total occlusion (CTO) represents one of the most challenging lesion subsets in coronary artery disease, and antegrade recanalization (AR) is the preferred approach for revascularization due to its lower complication risk. However, predicting AR success remains clinically difficult. The Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index (ALI), integrating body mass index, albumin, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, reflects nutritional and inflammatory status, both of which may influence procedural outcomes.

pmc-13428628.title: Delayed Presentation of a Retained Knife Fragment Following Penetrating Abdominal Trauma and Exploratory Laparotomy
pmc-13428628.creator: Joseph R Ragan, Alyssa Sinko, Katherine Selman
pmc-13428628.description: This case report describes a rare delayed presentation of a retained knife fragment following penetrating abdominal trauma and prior exploratory laparotomy. A 23-year-old male patient presented seven months after sustaining a stab wound with progressive left lower abdominal, buttock, and radicular leg pain, along with new-onset testicular discomfort.
